items.subject: math
items.skill: Theoretical probability of a simple event
items.prompt: A bag has 3 red, 5 blue, and 2 green marbles. One marble is drawn without looking. What is the probability that it is blue?

tip.en: Use a bag of colored objects or a coin and a die and try the experiment many times to compare with the fraction.

items.subject: math
items.skill: Probability of a compound event using a sample space
items.prompt: Grace flips a coin and rolls a fair six-sided die. What is the probability of getting heads and an even number?
items.explain: The sample space has 12 outcomes, and 3 of them (H2, H4, H6) match, so the probability is 3/12 = 1/4.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: What is the domain of f(x) = (x + 1)/(x² - 9)?
options: All real numbers except x = 3 and x = -3
items.explain: The denominator is zero when x = 3 or x = -3, so those values are excluded.

tip.en: Ask what value of x makes the denominator zero, because that is where trouble appears in the graph.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: The function g(x) = (x² - 4)/((x - 2)(x + 3)) has one vertical asymptote and one hole. At what value of x is the vertical asymptote?
items.explain: The factor x - 2 cancels, leaving a hole at x = 2; the factor x + 3 remains, so the asymptote is x = -3.

tip.en: Ask what value of x makes the denominator zero, because that is where trouble appears in the graph.
